papers.title_en: SE-MSB: End-to-End Unpaired Speech Enhancement using Mamba Schrödinger Bridges
papers.authors: Andreas Bagge, Andreas Nymand, Michael Riis Andersen, Bjørn Sand Jensen
papers.evidence: 扩散薛定谔桥用于非配对语音增强
papers.tldr: 语音增强通常依赖成对监督数据，将干净语音人工加噪，难以适应真实环境未知声学特性。本文提出完全非成对框架SE-MSB，用扩散薛定谔桥学习干净与退化语音分布间的随机传输，并设计高效Mamba扩散模型进行端到端波形处理。实验表明，其性能不逊或优于成对/非成对最先进方法及经典信号处理算法，推理速度快数个数量级，且能泛化到多种语音增强任务。该工作为真实场景语音修复提供了鲁棒高效的解决方案。
papers.abstract_en: Speech enhancement (SE) models typically rely on supervised learning with paired data examples where clean speech is synthetically degraded. This paradigm limits performance in real-world scenarios where the target environment's specific acoustic characteristics are unknown. We propose a fully unpaired SE framework that uses principled Diffusion Schrödinger Bridges (DSB) to learn a stochastic transport process between a clean and a degraded speech distribution. Algorithms for learning transport maps are computationally heavy since they require simulating differential equations during training, usually at each training step. Therefore, we propose using a high-efficiency Mamba Diffusion Model designed for end-to-end waveform processing. We compare against state-of-the-art methods for speech enhancement, both paired and unpaired, as well as a classical signal processing algorithm. Experimental results show that we are on par or better than the baselines while being orders of magnitude faster during inference. Furthermore, we show that the flexibility of the DSB formulation allows our model to generalize across SE tasks, offering a robust and efficient solution for real-world speech restoration.

papers.title_en: Bridge of $Ψ$'s: Quantum Circuit Optimization with Schrödinger Bridges
papers.authors: Lino S. Hofstetter, Lia Yeh, Prakash Murali
papers.evidence: 基于薛定谔桥的生成模型用于电路变换
papers.tldr: 量子电路优化旨在用更少门和更低深度替换原电路，以降低执行成本与错误率。现有方法多依赖固定重写库或刚性代数例程，难以从示例中泛化学习。作者提出 BOPS，一种基于薛定谔桥的生成模型，配自定义去噪器，直接学习从源电路到等价优化电路的变换。在 8 量子比特×64 深度 Clifford+T 留出集上，门数几何平均减少 2.46 倍，深度减少 2.45 倍，优于九个基线。这是首个桥接量子电路与前沿机器学习的生成模型，为量子编译栈开启可学习多轴优化。
papers.abstract_en: Quantum circuit optimization replaces a circuit with an equivalent one of fewer gates and lower depth, reducing execution cost and error rate. We ask whether a generative model can learn this transformation directly from examples, rather than selecting from a fixed rewrite library or rigid algebraic routines. We present Bridge of $Ψ$'s (BOPS), a generative model based on Schrödinger bridges, using a custom denoiser architecture, that learns a transformation from a source circuit into an equivalent optimized circuit. We train it on data constructed to be hard for existing optimizers, by applying rewrite rules backwards so that each input has a known lower-cost target. On held-out 8 qubits $\times$ 64 depth Clifford+$T$ circuits, BOPS reduces gate count by $2.46\times$ and depth by $2.45\times$ in geometric mean, outperforming all nine baseline optimizers. This constitutes the first generative model bridging quantum circuits and frontier machine learning methods, opening up the quantum compilation stack to learned optimization along multiple axes.

papers.title_en: Exact Simulation of Diffusions via Brownian Bridge Range Reconstruction
papers.evidence: 通过布朗桥范围重构精确模拟扩散桥
papers.tldr: 针对泊松势在两端无界时标量扩散路径与扩散桥的精确模拟问题，提出基于布朗桥极差重构的算法。方法通过采样布朗桥建议的最大值及其位置，以及相邻两个受限布朗游蛇的极值与位置，重构已实现极差；条件于这些有限信息，剩余路径分解为四个区间约束布朗桥并可在拒绝检验所需泊松时刻精确采样。算法无需时间离散化即可返回精确有限维骨架，并支持接受后任意有限时刻的精确细化。数值实验验证有限维分布，并指出受限游蛇极值模拟是非线性示例的主要计算开销。
papers.abstract_en: We develop an exact simulation algorithm for scalar diffusion paths and diffusion bridges when the Poisson potential is unbounded in both tails. The method reconstructs the realized range of a Brownian bridge proposal by sampling its maximum and location, together with the maxima and locations of the two adjacent restricted Brownian meanders. Conditional on this finite information, the remaining path decomposes into four conditionally independent interval-constrained Brownian bridges, which can be sampled exactly at the Poisson times required by the rejection test. In contrast to constructions based on an enclosing range layer, the proposed representation retains the exact extrema and their locations. Our algorithm returns an exact finite-dimensional skeleton without time-discretization error and permits exact post-acceptance refinement at arbitrary finite collections of times. Numerical experiments validate the resulting finite-dimensional laws and identify the restricted-meander extremum simulation as the principal computational cost in the nonlinear example.
